_comment: UP-10c menu (owner go 2026-11-04). One item = one (model + native thinking) pair Jev may pick. thinking: null = provider default (no field), else {control: effort|toggle, value}. Native values are policy data from effort-pairs-research (audit-code); the ones here are the 2026-10-22 measured levels until that lands. rank: higher = heavier/costlier (stickiness only switches DOWN after sticky.downgrade_after turns Jev rates simpler). backups: tried in order after the head, each with its own thinking; same model on another account/provider goes first once one is registered, then P2. gpt-6-luna is not on the menu (owner OK 2026-11-04). Specialists (S*, addendum 2026-11-04) carry requires_metering: true and stay off until menu.metering is true (warslop's pack-metering-per-model); P6's cost cutoff has until_metering: true and stops applying then. A specialist is picked only when Jev is confident about it AND about the task kind (menu.kinds), which must be one of its kinds. S2 (muse-wonder) is left out: it is on OpenRouter only (USD 4 in / 20 out per 1M) and the routers have no OpenRouter connection, so it cannot be dispatched. Specialist thinking is the provider default until effort-pairs-research measures them. S5 passes 1.00x already: set its requires_metering to false once the research confirms its quality. Item descriptions rewritten 2026-11-04 from the per-domain benchmark table (brief item 12), see ops/model-profiles.json.

kinds.general: an ordinary request: conversation, a question, an explanation, short writing or everyday code
kinds.expert_reasoning: expert level reasoning on a hard question that needs deep knowledge and careful judgement
kinds.business: business work: strategy, finance, reports, plans and decisions for a company
kinds.vision: a request about an image, photo, screenshot or scanned document
kinds.big_coding: a large coding job: a whole application, many files, a big refactor or a long build
kinds.long_documents: reading, comparing or summarising very long documents or many files at once
kinds.cybersecurity: computer security: vulnerabilities, attacks, defence, logs and incident analysis
kinds.automation: automating work through web services and APIs: connecting apps, webhooks, integrations and workflows
kinds.data_analysis: analysing data: tables, statistics, trends and charts from a dataset

items.label: Quick
items.description: quick answers with very little thinking: greetings, small talk, a single fact, a short rewrite or translation

items.label: Everyday
items.description: everyday requests with normal thinking: questions, explanations, summaries and writing, business and knowledge work, long documents

items.label: Careful expert
items.description: careful expert answers where the facts must be right: law, health, science and history; coding, web pages and charts; says plainly when it is unsure and takes its time

items.label: Deep reasoning
items.description: hard multi-step reasoning: maths, proofs, puzzles, difficult debugging and careful planning; thinks for a long time before answering

items.label: Agent and tools
items.description: multi-step work with tools: running code, reading and writing files, step by step tasks over many tool calls

items.label: Business and IT
items.description: business and IT work: reports, spreadsheets and office documents, diagnosing IT problems, computer security, everyday code

items.label: Expert reasoning
items.description: expert reasoning on hard questions, business analysis and decisions, reading images and professional reports, computer security

items.label: Big coding jobs
items.description: large coding jobs and long projects: a whole application, many files, a big refactor, long multi-step tool work

items.label: Long documents
items.description: very long documents and many files at once, computer security work, physics and scientific research code

items.label: Automation
items.description: automating online services and APIs: connecting apps, webhooks, integrations and step by step workflows

items.label: Data analysis
items.description: data analysis with Python: tables, statistics, trends and charts from a dataset; computer security; long medical documents

items.label: Quick
items.description: quick answers with very little thinking: greetings, small talk, a single fact, a short rewrite or translation

items.label: Normal
items.description: everyday chat and questions with normal thinking: explanations, writing and summaries, following instructions exactly

items.label: Think harder
items.description: requests that need careful step by step reasoning: maths, logic, science questions, tricky code; thinks longer before answering
